prompt.context: Assume you are the new pastor of a rural English church in the late nineteenth century. Over the last three years, attendance has been declining. Your boss has just come to town to tell you that she is considering shutting down the church. You have two weeks to diagnose the problem and come up with possible solutions.
prompt.question: How would you think through what these problems might be and the possible solutions?

framework: Competitive churches — location, religion/doctrine, services offered
General decline in churchgoing — progress/secularism, inconvenience/economic barriers
Testing hypotheses — talk to former parishioners, visit competing churches, map parishioner locations vs. church locations
Action plan — enhance services, increase flexibility of times/locations, improve accessibility

questions.prompt: What are the possible reasons for declining attendance?
questions.guidance: Strong answers structure causes into at least two buckets: (1) competition from other churches (better location, different religion/doctrine, better ancillary services such as childcare or adult education) and (2) secular/societal trends reducing overall churchgoing (scientific progress reducing reliance on religion, economic inconvenience such as parishioners needing to work the fields). Candidate should be explicit about the two-bucket structure and enumerate specific sub-hypotheses within each.

questions.prompt: How would you test your hypotheses?
questions.guidance: Interview former parishioners to understand why they left and what would bring them back. Visit competing churches during services to observe what is being preached and offered. Map current and former parishioners geographically and overlay competing churches to diagnose location effects.

questions.prompt: What actions would you recommend to reverse the decline?
questions.guidance: Focus on the needs of the parish. Offer enhanced services (e.g., daycare, adult education, singles events). Increase flexibility — services at different times of day. If distance is a barrier, hold services at multiple locations on a rotating basis to improve accessibility.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific services or changes could the church offer to attract parishioners back?

categories.name: Accessibility Improvements
ideas: Services at different times of day
Mobile/satellite services at locations closer to parishioner clusters
Transportation assistance for elderly or remote parishioners

categories.name: Spiritual & Pastoral
ideas: More personal attention and guidance from the pastor

categories.name: Competitive Differentiation
ideas: Understand and adapt to doctrinal preferences
Highlight unique community value vs. competing churches

recommendation: Conduct immediate outreach to former parishioners to diagnose the root causes of declining attendance before investing in any solutions
If competition is the driver, differentiate through superior community services (childcare, education, flexible schedules) and improve physical accessibility
If secular trends are the driver, focus on making church attendance more convenient and economically viable for working families
risks: Root cause may be irreversible secular trends rather than fixable service gaps
Resources (time, money, pastor bandwidth) may be insufficient to implement multiple changes in two weeks
Changes to doctrine or services may alienate remaining loyal parishioners
next_steps: Within the first week: interview at least 10–15 former parishioners and visit 2–3 competing churches
Map parishioner geography vs. church locations to quantify the distance effect
Bring findings and a prioritized action plan to the boss before the two-week deadline
